name: p1-dma-shared-profile-dma-f6
description: DMA replacement sample: the same pinned ZipDMA RTL selected through the shared_profile_dma declaration instead of zipdma_smoke, with its own test capability and its own behavior file carrying a declared capability block. F6 executes the four-word RAM block; the timer target declares no F5 facts, so F5 is refused by name while F1-F4 and F6 run.
notes: the DMA model is the same pinned ZipDMA RTL (third_party/soc-zipcpu, git:42606d2d6ef55df313772232977621b2d72f0159) that zipdma_smoke selects; the selected profile differs (component declaration, local harness block, test capability), and configs/behaviors/zipdma_capability_f6.json is that declaration's behavior file. This is a different profile over the same device, not a new device

the timer target declares no source_behavior and no inline F5 keys, so F5 is refused by name by the entry (unsupported-f5:target-irq-semantics:apb3:...) instead of being quietly skipped; F1-F4 and F6 still run

F6 is the four-word RAM block: the plan states dma_block_words 4, start word 0x00000000, LENGTH 16 bytes and full-word master strobes, and the case line reports the DMA master's own reads and writes plus the control-status word the ISR reads

the behavior file declares capabilities {channels 1, beat_bytes 4, max_outstanding 1, burst_beats 1}; the planner cross-checks them against the pinned device facts and the summary reports them beside the executed transfer. No capability above 1/4/1/1 is claimed or run
the target and DMA windows do not overlap: the timer owns 0x40001000..0x40001fff and the DMA control port 0x40003000..0x4000300f
